messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Smart-routing fallback loop detected (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Health-check flapping observed across regions. Auto-fallback policy invoked repeatedly. See /incidents/1827654321 for links.
alex.sre: paging oncall, this looks like the regional health-check state machine keeps flipping and routing tries to fall back to next region, which then fails and flips back. symptoms: elevated 5xx across multi-region frontends.
maria.eng: I'm seeing a recurring pattern where the fallback policy picks a lower-capacity variant (quantized replica) in us-west which then trips its health-check. the policy then jumps to eu, which is also busy -> loops back to us-east. timeline: starts ~1827654300.
karim-oncall: I'm on it. confirming page. starting with quick mitigation to stop routing churn.
alex.sre: +1. action 1: pause auto-fallback policy for impacted customer groups. action 2: set sticky routing to us-east for 60m. who can apply that change? jordan-prod?
jordan-prod: I can push a sticky route override to the SmartRouting service. patching now.
ops-bot: Deploy request received for service=smart-routing, change=sticky_override(us-east,60m), request_id=sr-1827. Applying to control-plane.
ops-bot: rollouts: control-plane config applied to 3 regions. waiting for prop propagation.
maria.eng: while that's in flight, can we also suppress health-check flapping alerts so Pager doesn't keep firing? we still need metrics though.
karim-oncall: Yes, I'll mute the repetitive health-check alert groups for 30m. muting alert-group=health-check-flap-rt.
alex.sre: Also, set fallback_throttle to 1 per 10m to prevent immediate chain. current config is unlimited.
jordan-prod: done: fallback_throttle set. config diff:
```
- fallback_throttle: 0
+ fallback_throttle: 1/600s
```
ops-bot: config updated for smart-routing v2.1. a/b rollout: 100% success.
sam-support: Customer impact: a handful of customers hitting high lat/5xx in eastbound requests, approx 12 tenant ids reported via support. triage now.
alex.sre: good. karim, keep an eye on token consumption and KV cache warmups in us-east (stickiness may spike cost but reduces churn).
karim-oncall: watching. metrics: 5xx dropped from 8% -> 1.2% after sticky override. routing churn graph flattened. health-check flaps still present in us-west but no longer causing cross-region failovers.
maria.eng: root cause hypoth: fallback policy was allowed to select "quantized-variant-v1" in us-west which has known intermittent startup failures with long sequence workloads. policy also had no hysteresis on health-checks. I captured logs showing fast fail-open transitions.
alex.sre: can we temporarily remove quantized-variant-v1 from fallback candidates until we have a fix? that should prevent picking the unstable variant.
jordan-prod: removing variant from candidate pool now: `PATCH /control-plane/v1/policies/{id}`. applied.
ops-bot: variant removal successful. policy now excludes quantized-variant-v1.
sam-support: notifying affected customers: drafting message. will post to status.redwood.ai once we confirm stability.
alex.sre: escalation: matrix/eng-ml and product on call pinged for post-mortem. maria, can you start an incident ticket and include eval prompt that triggers the failed path?
maria.eng: created INC-2026-482 with context and attached logs + grep output. linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/region-fallback
karim-oncall: handing off to alex for next shift. my shift ends in 30m. current status: stable with overrides in place, monitoring for 2h.
alex.sre: taking handoff. next steps: 1) bake policy changes into staging and add 10s hysteresis to health-checks 2) create test that simulates slow kv/cache warmups and long-seq load 3) schedule rollback window for sticky override 4) coordinate customer comms.
ops-bot: incident channel pinned: /incidents/1827654321. runbook steps initiated.
sam-support: posted initial status update to status.redwood.ai: "Partial degradation affecting multi-region routing; mitigation in progress."
jordan-prod: CI job scheduled to run canary traffic against new policy with variant exclusions.
maria.eng: note for post-mortem: we need a policy-level simulation harness that tests variant selection under load; right now selection logic lacks a capacity-safety check.
alex.sre: agree. also add a safety that a single region can't be evicted if the chosen fallback has <30% of original capacity.
karim-oncall: quick note: customer X (tenant: alpha-corp) reported degraded service at 1827654350. support ticket created TKT-9873.
sam-support: support ticket updated with mitigation steps and ETA 60m. customer acknowledged and asked for postmortem.
alex.sre: monitoring window extended. leaving sticky override for 60m now; will remove once hysteresis and variant exclusion verified.
ops-bot: metrics report link: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/xyz/region-fallback?org=redwood&id=1827654321
alex.sre: thanks all. I'll compile incident timeline and owners and post a full postmortem draft in #postmortems after analysis.
maria.eng: FYI I'll own the policy fix and a test harness. jordan, please coordinate with infra to repro quantized-variant startup instability.
jordan-prod: on it. will spawn a reproducible canary with long-seq prompt. assigning infra ticket INF-3245.
alex.sre: incident status -> MONITORING. root cause initial: fallback policy allowed unstable variant + health-check hysteresis too tight -> caused region health state oscillation -> smart-routing loop. mitigation: sticky override to us-east, throttle fallback, remove unstable variant, mute alerts.
karim-oncall: handing off closed. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=monitoring, priority=P1, incident_id=INC-2026-482, started_ts=1827654300, mitigated_ts=1827654460, owners=[alex.sre,maria.eng,jordan-prod], impact=partial_degradation_multi_region
alex.sre: closing the page. thanks everyone. will post postmortem in ~48h. :bow:
